column3: A Resilience4j `CircuitBreaker` is implemented via a finite state machine with three normal states, `CLOSED`, `OPEN` and `HALF_OPEN`, and three special states, `METRICS_ONLY`, `DISABLED` and `FORCED_OPEN` (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#introduction`).
column5: The CircuitBreaker is implemented via a finite state machine with three normal states: CLOSED, OPEN and HALF_OPEN and three special states METRICS_ONLY, DISABLED and FORCED_OPEN.

column3: The state of the `CircuitBreaker` changes from `CLOSED` to `OPEN` when the failure rate is equal or greater than a configurable threshold (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#failure-rate-and-slow-call-rate-thresholds`).
column5: The state of the CircuitBreaker changes from CLOSED to OPEN when the failure rate is equal or greater than a configurable threshold.

column3: After a wait time duration has elapsed, the `CircuitBreaker` changes from `OPEN` to `HALF_OPEN` and permits a configurable number of calls to see if the backend is still unavailable or has become available again (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#failure-rate-and-slow-call-rate-thresholds`).
column5: After a wait time duration has elapsed, the CircuitBreaker state changes from OPEN to HALF_OPEN and permits a configurable number of calls to see if the backend is still unavailable or has become available again.

column3: In `HALF_OPEN`, further calls are rejected with a `CallNotPermittedException` until all permitted calls have completed (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#failure-rate-and-slow-call-rate-thresholds`).
column5: Further calls are rejected with a CallNotPermittedException, until all permitted calls have completed.

column5: If the failure rate or slow call rate is then equal or greater than the configured threshold, the state changes back to OPEN.

column5: If the failure rate and slow call rate is below the threshold, the state changes back to CLOSED.

column3: The count-based sliding window aggregates the outcome of the last N calls, and the time-based sliding window aggregates the outcome of the calls of the last N seconds (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#introduction`).
column5: The count-based sliding window aggregrates the outcome of the last N calls. The time-based sliding window aggregrates the outcome of the calls of the last N seconds.

column3: The count-based sliding window is implemented with a circular array of N measurements (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#count-based-sliding-window`).
column5: The count-based sliding window is implemented with a circular array of N measurements.

column3: The time-based sliding window is implemented with a circular array of N partial aggregations, called buckets (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#time-based-sliding-window`).
column5: The time-based sliding window is implemented with a circular array of N partial aggregations (buckets).

column3: The time to retrieve a snapshot of a sliding window is constant, O(1), since the snapshot is pre-aggregated (`resilience4j-circuitbreaker#count-based-sliding-window`).
column5: The time to retrieve a Snapshot is constant O(1), since the Snapshot is pre-aggregated and is independent of the window size.
